first.rationale: Current data shows both onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ) declining. Memory_91 established that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action. This directly addresses the activation decline without the retention risk of promotional pricing (memory_73) or the narrow applicability of enterprise sales assist. Verifying memory_31 and memory_86 will confirm whether the onboarding decline is addressable through field simplification or shortening, but activation messaging is the immediate lever: it works on engaged users who are already in the product and can be deployed quickly. This preserves the option to address onboarding separately while tackling the steeper activation problem. Referral incentives work well for established customers (memory_57) but won't help new account activation velocity. Promotional pricing is ruled out due to retention risk and the need for sustainable revenue growth per primary objective.
